base..github/workflows/ci.yaml:
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]
  # Post-merge validation. Nothing else re-checks `main`, and branch protection
  # runs with `strict: false` — a PR need not be up to date to merge — so two
  # pull requests that each render cleanly in isolation can produce a `main`
  # that does not. A new Kustomization on one branch and a ConfigMap key
  # removed on the other is enough. Neither PR is wrong; the merge is.
  #
  # This cannot PREVENT that (a merge queue would; see the audit). What it does
  # is make it visible in two to three minutes, next to the commit that caused
  # it, instead of surfacing whenever someone next looks at a failing Flux
  # Kustomization on the cluster.
  push:
    branches: ["main"]

# Read-only by default. Every job below that checks out the PR runs PR code
# (pre-commit hooks, `task ci:*`, scripts/ci/*, render-both.sh), and the job
# token sits in that checkout's git config, readable by any of it. A write scope
# granted here reached all of them: `security-events: write` let a PR script
# dismiss code-scanning alerts repo-wide. The two write scopes CI needs live in
# `sarif-upload` and `render-diff-comment`, which never check out or run PR
# code: they download an artifact and hand it to a pinned action.
permissions:
  contents: read

# One in-flight run per PR. A push that supersedes an earlier commit cancels the
# run that was validating it — that run's verdict is about a commit nobody will
# merge, and branch protection waits on the newest run either way.
#
# Keyed on the workflow AND the ref, not the ref alone: `docs-check.yml` uses the
# same shape, and a shared group would have the two workflows cancelling each
# other on every push.
#
# CANCELLATION IS PULL-REQUEST ONLY, and that condition is the whole point of
# the post-merge trigger above. Every push to `main` is a DIFFERENT merge
# result, so a plain `cancel-in-progress: true` would let a second merge kill
# the run validating the first — and the commit that broke `main` would be
# precisely the one whose validation was thrown away. On `main` the runs queue.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Every job below carries `timeout-minutes: 15`. The whole pipeline runs in 2-3
# minutes, so 15 is not a budget — it is the point at which a job has stopped
# making progress (a hung `helm template`, a registry that accepts the connection
# and never answers). Without it the ceiling is GitHub's default of SIX HOURS,
# which holds a runner and leaves the PR showing a spinner rather than a failure.
jobs:
  pre-commit:
    name: Pre-commit checks 🛃
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Write required openbao files
        run: |
          mkdir -p opentofu/aws/openbao/cluster/.tls
          echo 'keep' > opentofu/aws/openbao/cluster/.tls/openbao.pem
          echo 'keep' > opentofu/aws/openbao/cluster/.tls/openbao-key.pem
          echo 'keep' > opentofu/aws/openbao/cluster/.tls/ca-chain.pem

      # Runs pre-commit directly rather than through the pre-commit-tf Dagger
      # module. That module cannot take a secret — its Run() accepts only
      # version, dir, tfBinary and a cache_dir wired to TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR —
      # so `tflint --init` fetched its ruleset from the GitHub releases API
      # unauthenticated, at 60 requests/hour shared across every Actions runner
      # on that egress IP. It failed on an unrelated docs PR on 2026-08-22.
      #
      # With GITHUB_TOKEN set below, tflint authenticates and gets 5000/hour.
      # The token is read-only (workflow-level `contents: read`), so a hook
      # that reads it gains nothing a public clone does not already have.
      # Tool versions come from mise.toml, which pins tofu, pre-commit and
      # tflint — the same file a contributor runs `mise install` against, so
      # this keeps the CI/local parity the Dagger image was there to provide.
      - name: Install tools
        uses: jdx/mise-action@2d8d4cafcbd33be2ea37d2b6f5ad595363d1f1ca # v5

      - name: Validate Opentofu configuration
        run: pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
        env:
          # tflint reads this when downloading the ruleset pinned in
          # .tflint.hcl. Without it the request is anonymous and rate-limited.
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # What the pre-commit-terraform hooks call instead of `terraform`.
          PCT_TFPATH: tofu

      - name: Test the OpenBao store-of-record module
        run: |
          tofu -chdir=opentofu/shared/modules/openbao-store-of-record init -backend=false -input=false
          tofu -chdir=opentofu/shared/modules/openbao-store-of-record test

  security-scan:
    name: Security scanning 🔒
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Run Trivy vulnerability scanner
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@ed142fd0673e97e23eac54620cfb913e5ce36c25 # v0.36.0
        with:
          scan-type: 'fs'
          scan-ref: '.'
          format: 'sarif'
          output: 'trivy-results.sarif'
          ignore-unfixed: true
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'

      - name: Run Checkov static analysis
        # Latest TAG, not latest RELEASE — the repo stopped cutting releases at
        # v12.1347.0 (whose old action.yml breaks on comma-separated framework)
        # but still tags every checkov bump.
        uses: bridgecrewio/checkov-action@6f26dc90000b74feb589a906cdfae540f5119895 # v12.3134.0
        with:
          directory: .
          quiet: true
          soft_fail: true
          framework: terraform,secrets
          output_format: sarif
          output_file_path: checkov-results.sarif

      # Handed to `sarif-upload`, which holds `security-events: write`. This job
      # runs Checkov over the PR tree (and Checkov reads a repo `.checkov.yaml`),
      # so it must not hold that scope itself.
      - name: Upload SARIF results for the upload job
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: sarif-results
          path: |
            trivy-results.sarif
            checkov-results.sarif
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      # The scan range has to come from the event. `base: main` / `head: HEAD`
      # is a real range on a pull request, where the two are different commits
      # — but on a push to `main` both resolve to the SAME commit, and the
      # action treats that as an error rather than a no-op:
      #
      #   BASE and HEAD commits are the same. TruffleHog won't scan anything.
      #
      # So this step failed on every merge while passing on every PR, which is
      # the one shape that defeats a post-merge check: green before, red after,
      # with nothing in the diff to explain it. It also kept the `ci-main-broken`
      # issue below permanently open, making that signal worthless. Observed on
      # 4e1f7523 and 36208b5e.
      #
      # `pull_request.base.sha` is empty on a push, so the fallback picks
      # `event.before` — the previous tip of `main`, which bounds exactly the
      # commits the merge introduced. `fetch-depth: 0` above is what makes both
      # ends reachable in the local clone.
      - name: Detect secrets with TruffleHog
        uses: trufflesecurity/trufflehog@e76dff8a7e57d6df0c60ad8cbf5d5cba505a8fc9 # v3.99.2
        with:
          path: ./
          base: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
          head: ${{ github.sha }}
          extra_args: --debug --only-verified

  # The only job with `security-events: write`. No checkout and no `run:`: it
  # downloads the SARIF that `security-scan` produced and uploads it with a
  # pinned action, so no PR code ever runs with this scope. Not a required
  # check; `Security scanning 🔒` remains the gate.
  sarif-upload:
    name: Upload SARIF results
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: security-scan
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - name: Download SARIF results
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8
        with:
          name: sarif-results

      # `category` keeps the configuration these results always had. Its default
      # is `<workflow>:<job id>`, so uploading from this job would file them
      # under `ci.yaml:sarif-upload`, orphaning every open alert on `main` and
      # leaving PRs with no base analysis to compare against.
      - name: Upload Trivy scan results to GitHub Security
        if: always()
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@b96794f015dfd88f77b49b1c93e0fa7110f94c63 # v4
        with:
          sarif_file: trivy-results.sarif
          category: .github/workflows/ci.yaml:security-scan

      - name: Upload Checkov scan results
        if: always()
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@b96794f015dfd88f77b49b1c93e0fa7110f94c63 # v4
        with:
          sarif_file: checkov-results.sarif
          category: .github/workflows/ci.yaml:security-scan

  kubernetes-validation:
    name: Kubernetes validation ☸
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7

      - name: Install tools
        uses: jdx/mise-action@2d8d4cafcbd33be2ea37d2b6f5ad595363d1f1ca # v5

      # Pinned: preflight.sh only enforces a version floor (>=0.10), so an
      # unpinned install silently floats to whatever upstream released.
      - name: Install the flux-schema plugin
        run: flux plugin install schema@0.11.0

      # render-bundle.py parses every rendered document; PyYAML happens to ship
      # in the runner image today, but that is not a dependency declaration.
      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: python3 -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check pyyaml

      # The test suites below need jq. Installed rather than assumed present on
      # the runner image, for the same reason as pyyaml above.
      - name: Install jq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq

      # NOTE: there is no "Install Polaris" step. Polaris comes from mise.toml
      # along with every other tool, because the upstream setup-polaris action
      # cannot install any release newer than 8.5.0 — see the comment on the
      # `polaris` pin in mise.toml for the naming change that broke it.

      # Charts are version-pinned, so only the download layer is cached (CL-2).
      # The bundle itself is always rendered fresh — a stale bundle is a
      # silently-wrong green, the exact failure class SPEC-007 removes.
      - name: Cache Helm chart downloads
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/helm
          # Glob every HelmRelease filename (helmrelease.yaml, helmrelease-*.yaml,
          # *-helmrelease.yaml), not just the exact name — ~17 releases use a
          # suffix and a version bump in those must still bust the cache.
          key: helm-${{ hashFiles('**/*helmrelease*.yaml', 'flux/sources/**') }}
          restore-keys: helm-

      # Every suite run.sh discovers, before the render: some of them test the
      # scripts that DO the render, and a broken resolve_values does not fail
      # validate-manifests.sh -- it quietly shrinks what that script checks.
      # Kept as their own step rather than folded into validate-manifests.sh,
      # whose contract is manifest validation.
      - name: Test suites
        run: task ci:test

      # Gate paths and pull_request secrets (SP3 SC-12, T8). In an existing required job:
      # a new required context could not be path-filtered and would need a settings change.
      # The scripts are called directly, not through the task wrappers: both scripts are gate
      # paths, the taskfiles are not, so an approved agent PR cannot turn this step into a no-op.
      - name: Merge-gate invariants
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: ./scripts/ci/check-policy-gate-coverage.sh && ./scripts/ci/check-workflow-secrets.sh

      # A pre-release crossplane-configuration pin has no release asset; its PR CI publishes the
      # XRD CRDs as an OCI artifact instead (SP2 ruling P40, review B2). A release pin exports
      # nothing, and gen-catalog.sh fetches the release asset as before.
      - name: Fetch the pinned pre-release's XRD CRDs
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          f="$(./scripts/ci/fetch-xrd-crds.sh)"
          [ -z "$f" ] || echo "XRD_CRDS_FILE=$f" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Runs even when a suite failed, so the manifest verdict is never hidden
      # behind it. The job still fails.
      - name: Validate manifests (flux schema + polaris)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: task ci:validate

  render-diff:
    name: Rendered manifest diff 📝
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # PULL REQUESTS ONLY. This job is meaningless on a push and would fail
    # outright: `github.base_ref` is empty outside a pull_request event, so the
    # render step would resolve `origin/` as its base revision. A diff against
    # `main` is also not a question a push TO `main` can ask.
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    # Informational only — never gates. GitOps: git is the source of truth, so
    # this diffs the rendered DESIRED state (main vs this PR). Drift (cluster ≠
    # git) is Flux's concern and is alerted on separately, so no cluster access
    # is needed here — keeping the job hosted, secretless and fork-safe.
    # Read-only: it runs the PR's render-both.sh and diff-bundles.py.
    # `render-diff-comment` posts the result.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install tools
        uses: jdx/mise-action@2d8d4cafcbd33be2ea37d2b6f5ad595363d1f1ca # v5

      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: python3 -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check pyyaml

      - name: Cache Helm chart downloads
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/helm
          key: helm-${{ hashFiles('**/*helmrelease*.yaml', 'flux/sources/**') }}
          restore-keys: helm-

      # Orchestration (concurrent best-effort renders, worktree, helm cache
      # isolation) lives in the script so it is shellcheck-covered and
      # documented next to the renderer it drives.
      - name: Render head and base (concurrent)
        run: ./scripts/ci/flux-schema/render-both.sh "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"

      # stdout (tee'd) is the size-capped PR comment; rendered-diff-full.md is
      # the full report (capped only by the job-summary limit, inside the
      # script, so a cut is boundary-aware and visibly noted), published two
      # ways: as the job summary — the human-readable page the comment's
      # truncation link points at — and as a downloadable artifact.
      - name: Compute rendered diff
        run: |
          python3 scripts/ci/flux-schema/diff-bundles.py /tmp/base/.bundle-base .bundle-head rendered-diff-full.md | tee rendered-diff.md
          cat rendered-diff-full.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # rendered-diff.md (the capped comment body) rides along for
      # `render-diff-comment`. `always()`: a partial diff is still posted, as
      # it was when the comment step lived in this job.
      - name: Upload full diff artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: rendered-diff
          path: |
            rendered-diff-full.md
            rendered-diff.md
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # The only job with `pull-requests: write`. No checkout and no `run:`: it
  # posts the comment `render-diff` computed, so no PR code runs with this
  # scope. Same-repo PRs only, as before.
  render-diff-comment:
    name: Post the rendered diff comment
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: render-diff
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Download the rendered diff
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8
        with:
          name: rendered-diff

      - name: Post/update PR comment
        uses: marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@5770ad5eb8f42dd2c4f34da00c94c5381e49af88 # v3.0.5
        with:
          header: rendered-manifest-diff
          path: rendered-diff.md

  shellcheck:
    name: Check the shell scripts 💻
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
      - name: Install ShellCheck
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y shellcheck
      - name: Run ShellCheck
        run: |
          # `-type l` as well as `-type f`, and it is load-bearing rather than
          # belt-and-braces. scripts/provision/openbao-snapshot.sh is a symlink (git mode
          # 120000) into container-images/openbao-snapshot/, and `-type f` tests
          # the LINK, not its target -- so the plain predicate matched 40 files
          # and silently skipped that one, the largest script in the tree.
          # Do not "simplify" this back to `-type f`.
          find ./scripts \( -type f -o -type l \) -name "*.sh" -print0 | xargs -0 shellcheck -x -S warning

  links:
    name: Check the documentation links 🔗
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
      - name: Resolve every relative Markdown link
        run: ./scripts/ci/validate-links.sh

      # Runs in this job rather than its own so the required-check list on
      # `main` does not have to change. The job name stays "documentation
      # links" for the same reason; it now gates documentation *claims* too.
      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: python3 -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check pyyaml

      - name: Check documentation claims against configuration
        run: ./scripts/ci/validate-doc-claims.sh

      # Folded into this job for the same reason as the claims check above: the
      # required-check list on `main` does not have to change.
      #
      # It runs HERE rather than in the shellcheck job because it needs the
      # pyyaml installed above. The shellcheck job installs only shellcheck, and
      # this repo does not treat "it happens to be in the runner image" as a
      # dependency declaration.
      - name: Check identity provider topology
        run: ./scripts/ci/validate-idp-topology.sh

      - name: OpenBao policy parity
        run: ./scripts/ci/validate-openbao-policies.sh

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Post-merge only. A red run on `main` is already visible next to the commit,
  # but only to someone looking at it -- and the whole point of the `push`
  # trigger above is to catch a break that NOBODY is looking for, because every
  # PR involved was green. So the failure has to come and find you.
  #
  # It files an issue rather than posting to Slack because this repository holds
  # no Slack webhook secret (`gh secret list`: AWS, Tailscale, Dagger, two LLM
  # keys -- no incoming webhook). An issue needs only the GITHUB_TOKEN that is
  # already here, so this adds no credential and nothing to rotate. If a webhook
  # is added later, notifying both is a two-line change; the point is that the
  # notification path must not itself be a thing to set up before this works.
  #
  # ONE issue, reopened and commented rather than duplicated. `main` staying
  # broken across several pushes is one incident, and a gate that files an issue
  # per push is a gate someone mutes.
  notify-main-broken:
    name: Report a broken main 🚨
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [pre-commit, security-scan, kubernetes-validation, shellcheck, links]
    # `failure()` is required: without it this inherits the default `success()`
    # and never runs. `render-diff` and `render-diff-comment` are deliberately
    # absent from `needs` -- they are pull-request-only and always skipped here.
    # `sarif-upload` is absent too: it gates nothing, and `security-scan`, which
    # it follows, is already listed.
    if: failure() && github.event_name == 'push'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Open or update the tracking issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # REQUIRED, because this job deliberately has no checkout step -- it
          # needs no code. Without it every `gh` call tries to infer the
          # repository from a local git remote, finds no `.git`, and dies with
          # `failed to run git: fatal: not a git repository`. Measured on the
          # first post-merge run: the notify job itself failed, which means a
          # broken `main` would have gone unreported -- the one outcome this job
          # exists to prevent. GH_REPO covers every gh invocation at once, so a
          # call added later cannot forget it the way a per-command --repo can.
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          LABEL: ci-main-broken
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          COMMIT_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/commit/${{ github.sha }}
          RESULTS: |
            - Pre-commit: ${{ needs.pre-commit.result }}
            - Security scanning: ${{ needs.security-scan.result }}
            - Kubernetes validation: ${{ needs.kubernetes-validation.result }}
            - Shell scripts: ${{ needs.shellcheck.result }}
            - Documentation: ${{ needs.links.result }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          body=$(cat <<EOF
          CI failed on \`main\` after a merge, so this is a break that every
          pull request involved reported as green.

          - Commit: ${COMMIT_URL}
          - Run: ${RUN_URL}

          Job results:
          ${RESULTS}

          The usual cause is two pull requests that are each valid alone and
          invalid together -- branch protection runs with \`strict: false\`, so
          neither was rendered against the other. Reproduce locally with
          \`./scripts/ci/validate-manifests.sh\` on \`main\`.
          EOF
          )

          # --force so a re-run is not a hard failure on "label already exists".
          gh label create "$LABEL" \
            --color b60205 \
            --description "CI is failing on main" \
            --force

          existing=$(gh issue list \
            --state open --label "$LABEL" --limit 1 \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')

          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            echo "main is already tracked as broken in #${existing}; commenting."
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body "$body"
          else
            gh issue create \
              --title "CI is failing on main" \
              --label "$LABEL" \
              --body "$body"
          fi
base..github/workflows/docs-check.yml:
name: Docs site

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]
    paths:
      - "website/**"
      - "docs/architecture/**"
      # Renovate bumps hugo-extended here on its own; without this the
      # site is never built against the new version before it reaches main.
      - "mise.toml"
      - "scripts/ci/verify-doc-paths.sh"
      - ".github/workflows/docs-check.yml"

permissions:
  contents: read

# Same shape as ci.yaml: one in-flight run per PR, keyed on workflow + ref so the
# two do not cancel each other.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build the documentation site 📚
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # enableGitInfo needs history

      - name: Install tools
        uses: jdx/mise-action@2d8d4cafcbd33be2ea37d2b6f5ad595363d1f1ca # v5

      - name: Cache Hugo modules
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/hugo_cache
          key: hugo-mod-${{ hashFiles('website/go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: hugo-mod-

      # refLinksErrorLevel: ERROR turns an unresolved relref into a non-zero
      # exit, so this step is the internal-link gate as well as the build gate.
      - name: Build
        working-directory: website
        run: hugo --minify --gc

      - name: Verify every referenced repository path exists
        run: ./scripts/ci/verify-doc-paths.sh
base..github/workflows/docs.yml:
name: Deploy docs site

on:
  push:
    branches: ["main"]
    paths:
      - "website/**"
      - "docs/architecture/**"
      # Renovate bumps hugo-extended here on its own; without this the
      # site is never built against the new version before it reaches main.
      - "mise.toml"
      - ".github/workflows/docs.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Never cancel an in-flight deploy: a half-published site is worse than a
# slightly stale one.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy to GitHub Pages 🚀
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install tools
        uses: jdx/mise-action@2d8d4cafcbd33be2ea37d2b6f5ad595363d1f1ca # v5

      - name: Cache Hugo modules
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/hugo_cache
          key: hugo-mod-${{ hashFiles('website/go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: hugo-mod-

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@45bfe0192ca1faeb007ade9deae92b16b8254a0d # v6

      - name: Build
        working-directory: website
        run: hugo --minify --gc

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5
        with:
          path: website/public

      - name: Deploy
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346 # v5

head..github/workflows/ci.yaml:
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]
  # Post-merge validation. Nothing else re-checks `main`, and branch protection
  # runs with `strict: false` — a PR need not be up to date to merge — so two
  # pull requests that each render cleanly in isolation can produce a `main`
  # that does not. A new Kustomization on one branch and a ConfigMap key
  # removed on the other is enough. Neither PR is wrong; the merge is.
  #
  # This cannot PREVENT that (a merge queue would; see the audit). What it does
  # is make it visible in two to three minutes, next to the commit that caused
  # it, instead of surfacing whenever someone next looks at a failing Flux
  # Kustomization on the cluster.
  push:
    branches: ["main"]

# Read-only by default. Every job below that checks out the PR runs PR code
# (pre-commit hooks, `task ci:*`, scripts/ci/*, render-both.sh), and the job
# token sits in that checkout's git config, readable by any of it. A write scope
# granted here reached all of them: `security-events: write` let a PR script
# dismiss code-scanning alerts repo-wide. The two write scopes CI needs live in
# `sarif-upload` and `render-diff-comment`, which never check out or run PR
# code: they download an artifact and hand it to a pinned action.
permissions:
  contents: read

# One in-flight run per PR. A push that supersedes an earlier commit cancels the
# run that was validating it — that run's verdict is about a commit nobody will
# merge, and branch protection waits on the newest run either way.
#
# Keyed on the workflow AND the ref, not the ref alone: `docs-check.yml` uses the
# same shape, and a shared group would have the two workflows cancelling each
# other on every push.
#
# CANCELLATION IS PULL-REQUEST ONLY, and that condition is the whole point of
# the post-merge trigger above. Every push to `main` is a DIFFERENT merge
# result, so a plain `cancel-in-progress: true` would let a second merge kill
# the run validating the first — and the commit that broke `main` would be
# precisely the one whose validation was thrown away. On `main` the runs queue.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Every job below carries `timeout-minutes: 15`. The whole pipeline runs in 2-3
# minutes, so 15 is not a budget — it is the point at which a job has stopped
# making progress (a hung `helm template`, a registry that accepts the connection
# and never answers). Without it the ceiling is GitHub's default of SIX HOURS,
# which holds a runner and leaves the PR showing a spinner rather than a failure.
jobs:
  pre-commit:
    name: Pre-commit checks 🛃
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Write required openbao files
        run: |
          mkdir -p opentofu/aws/openbao/cluster/.tls
          echo 'keep' > opentofu/aws/openbao/cluster/.tls/openbao.pem
          echo 'keep' > opentofu/aws/openbao/cluster/.tls/openbao-key.pem
          echo 'keep' > opentofu/aws/openbao/cluster/.tls/ca-chain.pem

      # Runs pre-commit directly rather than through the pre-commit-tf Dagger
      # module. That module cannot take a secret — its Run() accepts only
      # version, dir, tfBinary and a cache_dir wired to TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR —
      # so `tflint --init` fetched its ruleset from the GitHub releases API
      # unauthenticated, at 60 requests/hour shared across every Actions runner
      # on that egress IP. It failed on an unrelated docs PR on 2026-08-22.
      #
      # With GITHUB_TOKEN set below, tflint authenticates and gets 5000/hour.
      # The token is read-only (workflow-level `contents: read`), so a hook
      # that reads it gains nothing a public clone does not already have.
      # Tool versions come from mise.toml, which pins tofu, pre-commit and
      # tflint — the same file a contributor runs `mise install` against, so
      # this keeps the CI/local parity the Dagger image was there to provide.
      - name: Install tools
        uses: jdx/mise-action@08ae2a091c038e1e05ec6f5115dc5c69d5a2a6b8 # v5

      - name: Validate Opentofu configuration
        run: pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
        env:
          # tflint reads this when downloading the ruleset pinned in
          # .tflint.hcl. Without it the request is anonymous and rate-limited.
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # What the pre-commit-terraform hooks call instead of `terraform`.
          PCT_TFPATH: tofu

      - name: Test the OpenBao store-of-record module
        run: |
          tofu -chdir=opentofu/shared/modules/openbao-store-of-record init -backend=false -input=false
          tofu -chdir=opentofu/shared/modules/openbao-store-of-record test

  security-scan:
    name: Security scanning 🔒
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Run Trivy vulnerability scanner
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@ed142fd0673e97e23eac54620cfb913e5ce36c25 # v0.36.0
        with:
          scan-type: 'fs'
          scan-ref: '.'
          format: 'sarif'
          output: 'trivy-results.sarif'
          ignore-unfixed: true
          severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'

      - name: Run Checkov static analysis
        # Latest TAG, not latest RELEASE — the repo stopped cutting releases at
        # v12.1347.0 (whose old action.yml breaks on comma-separated framework)
        # but still tags every checkov bump.
        uses: bridgecrewio/checkov-action@6f26dc90000b74feb589a906cdfae540f5119895 # v12.3134.0
        with:
          directory: .
          quiet: true
          soft_fail: true
          framework: terraform,secrets
          output_format: sarif
          output_file_path: checkov-results.sarif

      # Handed to `sarif-upload`, which holds `security-events: write`. This job
      # runs Checkov over the PR tree (and Checkov reads a repo `.checkov.yaml`),
      # so it must not hold that scope itself.
      - name: Upload SARIF results for the upload job
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: sarif-results
          path: |
            trivy-results.sarif
            checkov-results.sarif
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      # The scan range has to come from the event. `base: main` / `head: HEAD`
      # is a real range on a pull request, where the two are different commits
      # — but on a push to `main` both resolve to the SAME commit, and the
      # action treats that as an error rather than a no-op:
      #
      #   BASE and HEAD commits are the same. TruffleHog won't scan anything.
      #
      # So this step failed on every merge while passing on every PR, which is
      # the one shape that defeats a post-merge check: green before, red after,
      # with nothing in the diff to explain it. It also kept the `ci-main-broken`
      # issue below permanently open, making that signal worthless. Observed on
      # 4e1f7523 and 36208b5e.
      #
      # `pull_request.base.sha` is empty on a push, so the fallback picks
      # `event.before` — the previous tip of `main`, which bounds exactly the
      # commits the merge introduced. `fetch-depth: 0` above is what makes both
      # ends reachable in the local clone.
      - name: Detect secrets with TruffleHog
        uses: trufflesecurity/trufflehog@e76dff8a7e57d6df0c60ad8cbf5d5cba505a8fc9 # v3.99.2
        with:
          path: ./
          base: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
          head: ${{ github.sha }}
          extra_args: --debug --only-verified

  # The only job with `security-events: write`. No checkout and no `run:`: it
  # downloads the SARIF that `security-scan` produced and uploads it with a
  # pinned action, so no PR code ever runs with this scope. Not a required
  # check; `Security scanning 🔒` remains the gate.
  sarif-upload:
    name: Upload SARIF results
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: security-scan
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - name: Download SARIF results
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8
        with:
          name: sarif-results

      # `category` keeps the configuration these results always had. Its default
      # is `<workflow>:<job id>`, so uploading from this job would file them
      # under `ci.yaml:sarif-upload`, orphaning every open alert on `main` and
      # leaving PRs with no base analysis to compare against.
      - name: Upload Trivy scan results to GitHub Security
        if: always()
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@b96794f015dfd88f77b49b1c93e0fa7110f94c63 # v4
        with:
          sarif_file: trivy-results.sarif
          category: .github/workflows/ci.yaml:security-scan

      - name: Upload Checkov scan results
        if: always()
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@b96794f015dfd88f77b49b1c93e0fa7110f94c63 # v4
        with:
          sarif_file: checkov-results.sarif
          category: .github/workflows/ci.yaml:security-scan

  kubernetes-validation:
    name: Kubernetes validation ☸
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7

      - name: Install tools
        uses: jdx/mise-action@08ae2a091c038e1e05ec6f5115dc5c69d5a2a6b8 # v5

      # Pinned: preflight.sh only enforces a version floor (>=0.10), so an
      # unpinned install silently floats to whatever upstream released.
      - name: Install the flux-schema plugin
        run: flux plugin install schema@0.11.0

      # render-bundle.py parses every rendered document; PyYAML happens to ship
      # in the runner image today, but that is not a dependency declaration.
      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: python3 -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check pyyaml

      # The test suites below need jq. Installed rather than assumed present on
      # the runner image, for the same reason as pyyaml above.
      - name: Install jq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq

      # NOTE: there is no "Install Polaris" step. Polaris comes from mise.toml
      # along with every other tool, because the upstream setup-polaris action
      # cannot install any release newer than 8.5.0 — see the comment on the
      # `polaris` pin in mise.toml for the naming change that broke it.

      # Charts are version-pinned, so only the download layer is cached (CL-2).
      # The bundle itself is always rendered fresh — a stale bundle is a
      # silently-wrong green, the exact failure class SPEC-007 removes.
      - name: Cache Helm chart downloads
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/helm
          # Glob every HelmRelease filename (helmrelease.yaml, helmrelease-*.yaml,
          # *-helmrelease.yaml), not just the exact name — ~17 releases use a
          # suffix and a version bump in those must still bust the cache.
          key: helm-${{ hashFiles('**/*helmrelease*.yaml', 'flux/sources/**') }}
          restore-keys: helm-

      # Every suite run.sh discovers, before the render: some of them test the
      # scripts that DO the render, and a broken resolve_values does not fail
      # validate-manifests.sh -- it quietly shrinks what that script checks.
      # Kept as their own step rather than folded into validate-manifests.sh,
      # whose contract is manifest validation.
      - name: Test suites
        run: task ci:test

      # Gate paths and pull_request secrets (SP3 SC-12, T8). In an existing required job:
      # a new required context could not be path-filtered and would need a settings change.
      # The scripts are called directly, not through the task wrappers: both scripts are gate
      # paths, the taskfiles are not, so an approved agent PR cannot turn this step into a no-op.
      - name: Merge-gate invariants
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: ./scripts/ci/check-policy-gate-coverage.sh && ./scripts/ci/check-workflow-secrets.sh

      # A pre-release crossplane-configuration pin has no release asset; its PR CI publishes the
      # XRD CRDs as an OCI artifact instead (SP2 ruling P40, review B2). A release pin exports
      # nothing, and gen-catalog.sh fetches the release asset as before.
      - name: Fetch the pinned pre-release's XRD CRDs
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: |
          f="$(./scripts/ci/fetch-xrd-crds.sh)"
          [ -z "$f" ] || echo "XRD_CRDS_FILE=$f" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Runs even when a suite failed, so the manifest verdict is never hidden
      # behind it. The job still fails.
      - name: Validate manifests (flux schema + polaris)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: task ci:validate

  render-diff:
    name: Rendered manifest diff 📝
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # PULL REQUESTS ONLY. This job is meaningless on a push and would fail
    # outright: `github.base_ref` is empty outside a pull_request event, so the
    # render step would resolve `origin/` as its base revision. A diff against
    # `main` is also not a question a push TO `main` can ask.
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    # Informational only — never gates. GitOps: git is the source of truth, so
    # this diffs the rendered DESIRED state (main vs this PR). Drift (cluster ≠
    # git) is Flux's concern and is alerted on separately, so no cluster access
    # is needed here — keeping the job hosted, secretless and fork-safe.
    # Read-only: it runs the PR's render-both.sh and diff-bundles.py.
    # `render-diff-comment` posts the result.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install tools
        uses: jdx/mise-action@08ae2a091c038e1e05ec6f5115dc5c69d5a2a6b8 # v5

      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: python3 -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check pyyaml

      - name: Cache Helm chart downloads
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/helm
          key: helm-${{ hashFiles('**/*helmrelease*.yaml', 'flux/sources/**') }}
          restore-keys: helm-

      # Orchestration (concurrent best-effort renders, worktree, helm cache
      # isolation) lives in the script so it is shellcheck-covered and
      # documented next to the renderer it drives.
      - name: Render head and base (concurrent)
        run: ./scripts/ci/flux-schema/render-both.sh "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"

      # stdout (tee'd) is the size-capped PR comment; rendered-diff-full.md is
      # the full report (capped only by the job-summary limit, inside the
      # script, so a cut is boundary-aware and visibly noted), published two
      # ways: as the job summary — the human-readable page the comment's
      # truncation link points at — and as a downloadable artifact.
      - name: Compute rendered diff
        run: |
          python3 scripts/ci/flux-schema/diff-bundles.py /tmp/base/.bundle-base .bundle-head rendered-diff-full.md | tee rendered-diff.md
          cat rendered-diff-full.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # rendered-diff.md (the capped comment body) rides along for
      # `render-diff-comment`. `always()`: a partial diff is still posted, as
      # it was when the comment step lived in this job.
      - name: Upload full diff artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: rendered-diff
          path: |
            rendered-diff-full.md
            rendered-diff.md
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  # The only job with `pull-requests: write`. No checkout and no `run:`: it
  # posts the comment `render-diff` computed, so no PR code runs with this
  # scope. Same-repo PRs only, as before.
  render-diff-comment:
    name: Post the rendered diff comment
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: render-diff
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Download the rendered diff
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8
        with:
          name: rendered-diff

      - name: Post/update PR comment
        uses: marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@5770ad5eb8f42dd2c4f34da00c94c5381e49af88 # v3.0.5
        with:
          header: rendered-manifest-diff
          path: rendered-diff.md

  shellcheck:
    name: Check the shell scripts 💻
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
      - name: Install ShellCheck
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y shellcheck
      - name: Run ShellCheck
        run: |
          # `-type l` as well as `-type f`, and it is load-bearing rather than
          # belt-and-braces. scripts/provision/openbao-snapshot.sh is a symlink (git mode
          # 120000) into container-images/openbao-snapshot/, and `-type f` tests
          # the LINK, not its target -- so the plain predicate matched 40 files
          # and silently skipped that one, the largest script in the tree.
          # Do not "simplify" this back to `-type f`.
          find ./scripts \( -type f -o -type l \) -name "*.sh" -print0 | xargs -0 shellcheck -x -S warning

  links:
    name: Check the documentation links 🔗
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
      - name: Resolve every relative Markdown link
        run: ./scripts/ci/validate-links.sh

      # Runs in this job rather than its own so the required-check list on
      # `main` does not have to change. The job name stays "documentation
      # links" for the same reason; it now gates documentation *claims* too.
      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: python3 -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check pyyaml

      - name: Check documentation claims against configuration
        run: ./scripts/ci/validate-doc-claims.sh

      # Folded into this job for the same reason as the claims check above: the
      # required-check list on `main` does not have to change.
      #
      # It runs HERE rather than in the shellcheck job because it needs the
      # pyyaml installed above. The shellcheck job installs only shellcheck, and
      # this repo does not treat "it happens to be in the runner image" as a
      # dependency declaration.
      - name: Check identity provider topology
        run: ./scripts/ci/validate-idp-topology.sh

      - name: OpenBao policy parity
        run: ./scripts/ci/validate-openbao-policies.sh

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Post-merge only. A red run on `main` is already visible next to the commit,
  # but only to someone looking at it -- and the whole point of the `push`
  # trigger above is to catch a break that NOBODY is looking for, because every
  # PR involved was green. So the failure has to come and find you.
  #
  # It files an issue rather than posting to Slack because this repository holds
  # no Slack webhook secret (`gh secret list`: AWS, Tailscale, Dagger, two LLM
  # keys -- no incoming webhook). An issue needs only the GITHUB_TOKEN that is
  # already here, so this adds no credential and nothing to rotate. If a webhook
  # is added later, notifying both is a two-line change; the point is that the
  # notification path must not itself be a thing to set up before this works.
  #
  # ONE issue, reopened and commented rather than duplicated. `main` staying
  # broken across several pushes is one incident, and a gate that files an issue
  # per push is a gate someone mutes.
  notify-main-broken:
    name: Report a broken main 🚨
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [pre-commit, security-scan, kubernetes-validation, shellcheck, links]
    # `failure()` is required: without it this inherits the default `success()`
    # and never runs. `render-diff` and `render-diff-comment` are deliberately
    # absent from `needs` -- they are pull-request-only and always skipped here.
    # `sarif-upload` is absent too: it gates nothing, and `security-scan`, which
    # it follows, is already listed.
    if: failure() && github.event_name == 'push'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Open or update the tracking issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # REQUIRED, because this job deliberately has no checkout step -- it
          # needs no code. Without it every `gh` call tries to infer the
          # repository from a local git remote, finds no `.git`, and dies with
          # `failed to run git: fatal: not a git repository`. Measured on the
          # first post-merge run: the notify job itself failed, which means a
          # broken `main` would have gone unreported -- the one outcome this job
          # exists to prevent. GH_REPO covers every gh invocation at once, so a
          # call added later cannot forget it the way a per-command --repo can.
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          LABEL: ci-main-broken
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          COMMIT_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/commit/${{ github.sha }}
          RESULTS: |
            - Pre-commit: ${{ needs.pre-commit.result }}
            - Security scanning: ${{ needs.security-scan.result }}
            - Kubernetes validation: ${{ needs.kubernetes-validation.result }}
            - Shell scripts: ${{ needs.shellcheck.result }}
            - Documentation: ${{ needs.links.result }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          body=$(cat <<EOF
          CI failed on \`main\` after a merge, so this is a break that every
          pull request involved reported as green.

          - Commit: ${COMMIT_URL}
          - Run: ${RUN_URL}

          Job results:
          ${RESULTS}

          The usual cause is two pull requests that are each valid alone and
          invalid together -- branch protection runs with \`strict: false\`, so
          neither was rendered against the other. Reproduce locally with
          \`./scripts/ci/validate-manifests.sh\` on \`main\`.
          EOF
          )

          # --force so a re-run is not a hard failure on "label already exists".
          gh label create "$LABEL" \
            --color b60205 \
            --description "CI is failing on main" \
            --force

          existing=$(gh issue list \
            --state open --label "$LABEL" --limit 1 \
            --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')

          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            echo "main is already tracked as broken in #${existing}; commenting."
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body "$body"
          else
            gh issue create \
              --title "CI is failing on main" \
              --label "$LABEL" \
              --body "$body"
          fi
head..github/workflows/docs-check.yml:
name: Docs site

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main"]
    paths:
      - "website/**"
      - "docs/architecture/**"
      # Renovate bumps hugo-extended here on its own; without this the
      # site is never built against the new version before it reaches main.
      - "mise.toml"
      - "scripts/ci/verify-doc-paths.sh"
      - ".github/workflows/docs-check.yml"

permissions:
  contents: read

# Same shape as ci.yaml: one in-flight run per PR, keyed on workflow + ref so the
# two do not cancel each other.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build the documentation site 📚
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # enableGitInfo needs history

      - name: Install tools
        uses: jdx/mise-action@08ae2a091c038e1e05ec6f5115dc5c69d5a2a6b8 # v5

      - name: Cache Hugo modules
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/hugo_cache
          key: hugo-mod-${{ hashFiles('website/go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: hugo-mod-

      # refLinksErrorLevel: ERROR turns an unresolved relref into a non-zero
      # exit, so this step is the internal-link gate as well as the build gate.
      - name: Build
        working-directory: website
        run: hugo --minify --gc

      - name: Verify every referenced repository path exists
        run: ./scripts/ci/verify-doc-paths.sh

name: Deploy docs site

on:
  push:
    branches: ["main"]
    paths:
      - "website/**"
      - "docs/architecture/**"
      # Renovate bumps hugo-extended here on its own; without this the
      # site is never built against the new version before it reaches main.
      - "mise.toml"
      - ".github/workflows/docs.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Never cancel an in-flight deploy: a half-published site is worse than a
# slightly stale one.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy to GitHub Pages 🚀
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install tools
        uses: jdx/mise-action@08ae2a091c038e1e05ec6f5115dc5c69d5a2a6b8 # v5

      - name: Cache Hugo modules
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/hugo_cache
          key: hugo-mod-${{ hashFiles('website/go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: hugo-mod-

      - name: Configure Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@45bfe0192ca1faeb007ade9deae92b16b8254a0d # v6

      - name: Build
        working-directory: website
        run: hugo --minify --gc

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@fc324d3547104276b827a68afc52ff2a11cc49c9 # v5
        with:
          path: website/public

      - name: Deploy
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@368f82528645a54fb793d4d04e342629a3f51346 # v5
